question: Which of the following non-metals is found liquid at room temperature?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bromine**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bromine** is the only non-metal that exists as a liquid at room temperature (approximately 25°C).
 
• It has a **melting point of -7.2°C** and a **boiling point of 58.8°C**, which means it remains in the liquid state under standard room conditions.
 
• **Bromine** is a reddish-brown liquid with a pungent odor and is highly volatile, forming toxic fumes.
 
• It belongs to the **halogen group (Group 17)** of the periodic table, which also includes fluorine, chlorine, iodine, and astatine.
 
• Bromine is widely used in industries for the production of **flame retardants, pesticides, and dyes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Iodine**:

 
 
• Iodine is a solid at room temperature and has a melting point of 113.7°C and a boiling point of 184.3°C.
 
• It is primarily used in **iodized salt** and as an antiseptic in medicines.
 
• Iodine is a member of the halogen group and exists in a crystalline form with a metallic luster.
 
 
 
• **Nitrogen**:
 
 
• Nitrogen is a gas at room temperature with a boiling point of -195.8°C and a melting point of -210°C.
 
• It makes up approximately **78% of Earth's atmosphere** and is essential for the formation of amino acids and proteins in living organisms.
 
• Nitrogen is used industrially in the production of fertilizers, explosives, and as a cryogenic agent.
 
 
 
• **Phosphorus**:
 
 
• Phosphorus exists in several allotropes, with **white phosphorus** and **red phosphorus** being the most common.
 
• At room temperature, phosphorus is a solid with a melting point of 44.1°C (white phosphorus).
 
• It is widely used in the production of fertilizers, explosives, and matches.
 
 
 
• **Bromine**:
 
 
• Bromine is a unique non-metallic element because it is a liquid at room temperature.
 
• Its applications include **fire retardants, water treatment chemicals, and photographic films.**
 
• Bromine is toxic and corrosive, requiring careful handling and storage.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Unique Properties of Bromine:**

 
 
• Bromine's liquid state at room temperature is a result of its moderate intermolecular forces, specifically **van der Waals forces.**
 
• It is highly reactive and forms compounds with a wide range of elements.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Halogens:**
 
 
• Other halogens such as chlorine and fluorine are gases at room temperature, while iodine and astatine are solids.
 
• This variability in physical states among halogens is due to differences in atomic mass and intermolecular forces.
 
 
 
• **Safety Precautions:**
 
 
• Bromine is highly toxic and can cause severe burns upon contact with the skin.
 
• Proper ventilation, protective clothing, and equipment are essential when handling bromine.
